notes: Only public, tourist-friendly places verified on official tourism sources. Descriptions are our own. Every stop needs review before launch.

trails.title: Gangneung coast: BTS, Goblin & the fish market
trails.difficulty: Easy: flat beach walks, with a short taxi or bus ride between some stops
trails.bestSeason: Spring to autumn. The coast is cold and windy in winter.
gettingThere: Take a KTX train from Seoul to Gangneung Station.
From Gangneung Station, city buses 300, 302 and 314 run north toward Jumunjin. Check current routes at the station, as this comes from a 2019 guide.
A taxi from Gangneung Station to the first stop is the simplest option.
trails.respectNote: Jumunjin is a working fishing town. Keep photo stops short, don't block the harbor, piers or market stalls, and take your trash with you.

stops.name: BTS Bus Stop at Hyangho Beach
stops.why: A rebuilt version of the seaside bus stop set from a BTS album shoot. It isn't a real bus stop.
stops.reviewNote: KTO's English page names the album 'Young Forever (2016)'; KTO's Korean pages say the 2017 repackage, 'You Never Walk Alone'.

stops.name: Sodol Adul Rock Park
stops.why: Odd-shaped sea rocks with a local wish-making legend, and a short coastal walk.
stops.hours: Until 7 PM (April–October). No evening entry because it's a military area. From a 2019 KTO guide, so check before you go.

stops.name: Sodol Port red lighthouse
stops.why: A small harbor with a red lighthouse and breakwater that appears in the drama.

stops.name: Jumunjin Fish Market
stops.why: The east coast's biggest seafood market, running since 1936. Buy fresh or dried seafood, or eat sashimi on the spot.

stops.name: Yeongjin Beach breakwater (Goblin filming spot)

relatedWork.title: Guardian: The Lonely and Great God (Goblin)

stops.why: The breakwater where the drama's leads first meet. Fans still come to take photos here.
stops.reviewNote: VisitKorea English calls this 'Jumunjin Breakwater' (1609 Haean-ro); KTO Korean says it is a breakwater at Yeongjin Beach. Confirm both point to the same spot.

trails.title: Busan on screen: Nampo markets to Huinnyeoul
trails.difficulty: Easy in Nampo. Huinnyeoul sits on a cliff, with steep alleys and stairs.
trails.bestSeason: Year-round. The Busan International Film Festival takes over BIFF Square every autumn.
gettingThere: Take a KTX train to Busan Station, then Busan Metro Line 1 to Nampo Station.
BIFF Square is about 5 minutes on foot from Nampo Station Exit 3.
For Huinnyeoul, take bus 7, 71 or 508 from near Nampo Station Exit 6 to the 영선동 백련사 (Yeongseon-dong Baengnyeonsa) stop.
trails.respectNote: Huinnyeoul is a village where people live. Keep your voice down, don't go into private homes, gardens or doorways, don't photograph residents, and avoid visiting late in the day.

stops.name: BIFF Square
stops.why: The street where Busan's film festival started in 1996, with filmmakers' handprints set in the pavement and lots of street food.

stops.name: Gukje Market
stops.why: A huge, maze-like market that grew up after the Korean War. The family shop from the film is still a popular photo stop.

stops.name: Jagalchi Market
stops.why: One of Korea's biggest fish markets. The alleys around it are full of grilled-fish and eel restaurants.
stops.hours: 05:00–22:00. Closed on the 1st, 3rd and 5th Tuesday of each month.

stops.name: Huinnyeoul Culture Village
stops.why: Narrow alleys on a sea cliff with small cafes, workshops and open sea views, plus the coastal walking path below.
stops.hours: Village open daily. Info center (film archive) 10:00–18:00, closed Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok. Please avoid late visits.

trails.title: Old Seoul: palace, hanok alleys & Gwangjang Market
trails.difficulty: Easy to moderate: mostly walking, with some steep lanes in Bukchon. One short subway ride at the end.
trails.bestSeason: Spring and autumn. Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays.
gettingThere: Take Seoul Subway Line 3 to Gyeongbokgung Station for the palace.
Bukchon is a short walk east of the palace. Anguk Station (Line 3) is the nearest stop.
Ikseon-dong is about 3 minutes on foot from Jongno 3(sam)-ga Station Exit 6 (Lines 1, 3, 5).
For Gwangjang Market, use Jongno 5(o)-ga Station Exit 7 (Line 1), one stop east, or walk about 15 minutes.
trails.respectNote: Bukchon is a neighborhood where people live. Tourists may visit the Bukchon-ro 11-gil area only from 10:00 to 17:00. Keep quiet, don't open gates or sit on doorsteps, and don't photograph residents.

stops.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
stops.why: The largest of Seoul's five Joseon palaces, built in 1395. Entry is free if you wear hanbok.
stops.hours: 09:00–17:00 (Nov–Feb), 09:00–18:00 (Mar–May, Sep–Oct), 09:00–18:30 (Jun–Aug). Last entry 1 hour before closing. Closed Tuesdays.
stops.cost: 3,000 won for adults. Free under 19 and over 65.
stops.reviewNote: Free entry in hanbok is widely reported but not on the VisitKorea page; confirm on the Royal Palaces site (royal.khs.go.kr).

stops.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
stops.why: Hundreds of tile-roofed hanok houses on hills between two palaces, once home to Joseon nobles.
stops.hours: Tourist visits 10:00–17:00 on Bukchon-ro 11-gil. Fines may apply outside these hours.

stops.name: Ikseon-dong Hanok Street
stops.kind: Hanok alleys with cafes and shops
stops.why: Seoul's oldest hanok neighborhood: narrow alleys of small hanok turned into cafes, restaurants and shops.

stops.name: Gwangjang Market
stops.why: Korea's first permanent market, opened in 1905. Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancake) and mini gimbap.
stops.hours: Shops 09:00–18:00, closed Sundays. Food street 09:00–23:00, open all year.

trails.title: Jeonju: hanok village, royal shrine & night market
trails.estimatedTime: 4–5 hours (plus the night market on Fri/Sat)
trails.difficulty: Easy: flat streets, with a short climb up to Omokdae.
trails.bestSeason: Year-round. Spring and autumn are nicest. Come on a Friday or Saturday for the night market.
gettingThere: Take a KTX train from Seoul (Yongsan) to Jeonju Station, or an express bus to Jeonju Express Bus Terminal.
From Jeonju Station, city buses 79, 119, 535 and 1000 go toward the Hanok Village (about 30 minutes). Check current routes at the station, as this comes from an older guide.
A taxi from Jeonju Station takes about 20 minutes. On weekends the village streets are closed to cars, so you'll walk in from the edge.
trails.respectNote: Many hanok here are homes and guesthouses. Keep your voice down in the side alleys, and be quiet inside Jeondong Cathedral, which is an active church.

stops.name: Jeondong Catholic Cathedral
stops.why: A red-and-gray brick church from 1914, built where Korea's first Catholic martyrs died. It stands out among the hanok rooftops.
stops.hours: Active church with daily Mass. Visit quietly outside Mass times.
stops.reviewNote: VisitKorea lists only Mass times; confirm tourist visiting hours with the cathedral (jeondong.or.kr).

stops.name: Gyeonggijeon Shrine
stops.why: Holds the portrait of King Taejo, founder of the Joseon dynasty, which began in Jeonju. Bamboo groves and old trees inside.
stops.hours: 09:00–18:00 (Nov–Feb), 09:00–19:00 (Mar–May, Sep–Oct), 09:00–20:00 (Jun–Aug). Last entry 1 hour before closing. Open all year.
stops.cost: 3,000 won for adults (25–64). Free on the last Wednesday of the month.

stops.name: Omokdae Pavilion
stops.why: Where the future King Taejo celebrated a victory in 1380. Walk up for a view over the hanok rooftops, especially at night.

stops.name: Nambu Market & night market
stops.why: Jeonju's biggest market, over 100 years old. Eat kongnamul-gukbap (bean sprout soup) by day, or street food at the night market.
stops.hours: Night market Fridays and Saturdays, 17:00–23:00 (Jeonju city, 2023). Check before you go.
stops.reviewNote: Night market hours come from a Dec 2023 Jeonju city post; other sources say until 24:00.

trails.title: Jeju east coast: Sunrise Peak & When Life Gives You Tangerines
trails.difficulty: Moderate: the climb up Seongsan Ilchulbong takes 30–40 minutes on stairs. The rest is flat coastal walking.
trails.bestSeason: Spring, when the canola flowers bloom. The peak closes in bad weather.
gettingThere: From Jeju Airport, take express bus 101 (Platform 2, in front of Gate 2 on the 1st floor) to Seongsan Ilchulbong.
City bus 201 also runs along the east coast. It is slower but stops at most attractions, including Gwangchigi Beach.
Jeju buses don't take cash (since October 2024). Pay with a transit card or a QR code.
Gwangchigi Beach is about 20 minutes on foot from the peak, and Seopjikoji is a short taxi ride further south.
trails.respectNote: These are protected natural sites. Stay on the paths, don't climb the rocks or take stones, and don't bother the haenyeo (women divers) at work.

stops.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak)
stops.why: A 182 m volcanic cone rising from the sea, with a huge crater at the top. Famous for sunrise views.
stops.hours: 06:00–18:00 (Nov–Feb), 05:00–19:00 (Mar–Apr, Sep–Oct), 04:30–20:00 (May–Aug). Last ticket 1 hour before closing. Closed the first Monday of each month.
stops.cost: Free coastal path. 5,000 won to climb to the summit.
stops.reviewNote: Summit fee (5,000 won) is from VisitKorea search text; VisitJeju page does not state the amount.

stops.name: Gwangchigi Beach
stops.why: Black volcanic sand and green, moss-covered lava rocks at low tide, with the peak behind. A top sunrise photo spot.
stops.reviewNote: VisitJeju's Tangerines page names this beach as a nearby spot / Olle 1 end, not clearly as a filming location, so no drama link is shown.

stops.name: Seopjikoji
stops.why: A grassy cape of red volcanic rock with a lighthouse, canola fields in spring, and views back to Sunrise Peak.
